A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same survey. Their complete 59-page and 61-page contents, including figures, tables, equations, and references, support comparison. Neither contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 report the authors' original memory and computational profiling of BERT-family and LLaMA models, with outcomes in Figures 7–8.

after.justification: The original profiling results in Sections 3.3–3.4 and Figures 7–8 are retained. Figure 7 additionally documents measurement settings.

M1.justification: The paper's taxonomy and illustrated fine-tuning procedures remain unchanged. FedPruner, DevFT, and SmartFed are newly surveyed contributions from cited work, not new components of an algorithm proposed by this paper.

E1.justification: No change to training or evaluation task coverage is reported for the original profiling. Section 5 consolidates or edits catalogued resources, including the BELLE entries, but these resources are surveyed rather than newly used in experiments.

E2.justification: The corresponding model comparison sets in Figures 5, 7, and 8 are unchanged. Added methods in Tables 2–3 receive literature summaries and challenge classifications, not experimental comparisons against a proposed method.

E3.justification: The stated profiling procedures, including the FLOPs measurement batch size of 16, are retained. Figure 7 newly discloses settings without establishing a protocol revision. Changes to Section 5's descriptions of external benchmark metrics do not document changes to experiments performed by this work.

E4.justification: The resource comparisons and schematic discussion of heterogeneity are retained. No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, error analyses, or case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its profiling results.

E6.justification: The profiling outcomes remain unchanged: Figure 7 reports 51.85 GB for LLaMA2-7B and 98.56 GB for LLaMA2-13B in both versions, and Figure 8 retains the 103.07-fold FLOPs ratio for LLaMA2-13B versus BERT. No new empirical benchmark scores are reported.

T1.justification: The transformer, LoRA, prompt-tuning, and adapter formulations remain mathematically equivalent, including Equations 1–7. No new assumptions, theoretical results, derivations, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same comprehensive-survey claim, five-category taxonomy, four principal challenges, evaluation-resource framework, applications, and future research agenda.

C2.justification: Interpretations of resource bottlenecks and the substantive limitations and future directions remain unchanged. The expanded personalized-FL description and explicit attribution of the Ollama example to a news outlet clarify existing discussion without introducing new mechanisms or applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Figure 7 adds the NVIDIA H800 hardware, FP32/FP16 precisions, batch size 16, and maximum sequence length 512. The resource tables add direct dataset and benchmark links and revise technical summaries. For example, Long2RAG's listed criteria change from key-point recall and LLM-based assessments to BLEU, ROUGE, and exact match; this is documentation rather than a reported experimental change.

R1.justification: Section 4.1.2 and Tables 2–3 add FedPruner, DevFT, and SmartFed. Additional background references include personalized-FL and memory-efficiency work. These updates extend the literature review within its existing scope and positioning; duplicate-reference consolidation and publication updates do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: Section 5's extensive tabulated descriptions, evaluation objectives, and metric summaries are systematically rewritten into compact phrases and standardized labels. This substantial editorial revision is concentrated in the catalogues; the eight-section organization and most narrative paragraphs remain intact. Author information, acknowledgements, terminology, and several explanatory passages also change.

P2.justification: The densely compressed v2 Tables 9–11 become six substantially more legible tables in v3: Tables 9–10, 11–12, and 13–14 respectively. Domain grouping, typography, captions, and placement change, alongside the journal-format title page and headers. Tables 2–3 gain literature rows, while the existing figures are retained with limited caption edits.

improvement.justification: V3 clearly improves table legibility, resource access, profiling documentation, and literature currency. However, substantive benchmark-metric revisions remain unexplained. For CitaLaw, v2 Table 11 agrees with the prose on syllogism alignment and legal consistency; v3 Table 14 instead lists MRR, recall, and ROUGE while Section 5.2.6 retains the earlier description. The PDFs do not reconcile these accounts, leaving the technical reliability of the revised evaluation guide—and the net quality improvement—uncertain.
